editorNote: Three threads today: Rocket Lab converts its space ambitions into recurring government revenue with a nine-figure Space Force award, Wall Street turns more skeptical on Duolingo just hours ahead of its earnings print, and Coinkite's admission that its own AI-assisted audits missed the bug behind the Coldcard hack adds a cautionary note as crypto's losses there climb past $130 million.

stories.headline: Rocket Lab wins $397 million Space Force contract to build and fly 'Flatellite' satellites
stories.summary: The U.S. Space Force awarded Rocket Lab a $397 million contract under its Space-Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator program to design, build, launch, and operate a constellation of flat-panel 'Flatellite' satellites. The spacecraft are slated to launch on Rocket Lab's still-unflown Neutron rocket, and the contract value includes an option for additional satellites.
stories.whyItMatters: It extends Rocket Lab's shift from launch provider to end-to-end space contractor with recurring satellite-operations revenue, and adds another payload to Neutron's manifest before its first flight.

sourceLinks.title: Rocket Lab Awarded $397 Million Contract to Build and Launch Flatellites for U.S. Space Force's SB-AMTI Program

stories.headline: Bank of America downgrades Duolingo to Underperform, cuts price target to $93, hours before Q2 earnings
stories.summary: BofA analyst Omar Dessouky moved Duolingo from Neutral to Underperform and lowered his price target from $103 to $93, arguing the stock trades at a roughly six-times premium to midcap subscription peers with similar EBITDA growth. The firm also cut its 2027 bookings-growth estimate to 9% from 11% and trimmed projected EBITDA to $338 million from $388 million, citing uncertainty around a planned, voice-focused app redesign.
stories.whyItMatters: The downgrade lands just hours before Duolingo reports second-quarter results after today's close, giving investors a bearish counterpoint heading into the print.

stories.headline: Coldcard maker says its own AI code review missed the bug behind the $130M hardware-wallet hack
stories.summary: Coinkite said total losses from the Coldcard firmware exploit have grown to roughly $130 million across four attack waves, per Galaxy Research estimates, and disclosed that AI-assisted reviews of its codebase — including one run weeks before the exploit — failed to catch the flaw. The company said it retested the code afterward against several frontier AI models, and none of them caught it either.
stories.whyItMatters: It undercuts the case that AI-assisted audits can substitute for human review of security-critical code, and pushes the running Coldcard loss total well past the roughly $100 million reported a day earlier.
